post.description: Authenticate a user and create an authentication session. Web clients receive the access token in JSON and refresh/CSRF tokens through cookies. Mobile clients receive both access and refresh tokens in JSON.

client_type.description: Client type. Defaults to web if omitted.

remember_me.description: Whether to create a persistent authentication session.

200.description: Successful login. Web clients receive refresh_token and XSRF-TOKEN cookies. The refresh_token cookie is HttpOnly; the XSRF-TOKEN cookie is accessible to JavaScript. Mobile clients receive refresh_token in the JSON response instead.

refresh_token.description: Returned only to mobile clients. Web clients receive this token through an HttpOnly cookie.

post.description: Log out the authenticated user from the current device. The current authentication session and its associated refresh tokens are revoked, and the current JWT access token is invalidated. For web clients, the refresh_token and XSRF-TOKEN cookies are also cleared.

200.description: Successful logout. For web clients, the refresh_token and XSRF-TOKEN cookies are expired.

Set-Cookie.description: Web clients receive expired refresh_token (HttpOnly) and XSRF-TOKEN cookies. Mobile clients do not use these cookies.

401.description: Unauthenticated - Invalid or expired access token.

post.description: Refresh the access token using an independent refresh token. Web clients must send the refresh_token HttpOnly cookie, the XSRF-TOKEN cookie, the matching X-CSRF-TOKEN header, and an allowed Origin header. Mobile clients must send the refresh token through the Authorization Bearer header. Exactly one refresh token source must be provided. Every successful refresh rotates the refresh token. The CSRF token remains unchanged during refresh.

parameters.name: refresh_token
parameters.description: Web only. HttpOnly refresh token cookie. Do not send this together with the Authorization Bearer header.

parameters.name: XSRF-TOKEN
parameters.description: Web only. JavaScript-readable signed CSRF cookie.

parameters.name: Authorization
parameters.description: Mobile only. Send the refresh token as a Bearer token.

parameters.name: X-CSRF-TOKEN
parameters.description: Web only. Must exactly match the XSRF-TOKEN cookie.

parameters.name: Origin
parameters.description: Web only. Must match the configured frontend origin.

200.description: Access token refreshed successfully. Mobile clients receive the rotated refresh token in JSON. Web clients receive it through a new HttpOnly cookie. The existing XSRF-TOKEN cookie is not rotated.

Set-Cookie.description: Web only. Contains the rotated refresh_token cookie with HttpOnly enabled.

refresh_token.description: Rotated refresh token. Returned only to mobile clients; web clients receive it through an HttpOnly cookie.

401.description: Invalid, expired, revoked, reused, or missing refresh token. Also returned when both refresh token sources are provided.

419.description: CSRF token mismatch. The XSRF-TOKEN cookie and X-CSRF-TOKEN header must contain the same valid signed token.

302.description: Redirect to the frontend email verification page. The status query parameter indicates the verification result.
